language.name: English
menu.title: MAIN MENU
menu.scan.description: Inspects your PC without changing anything and reports what needs your attention.
menu.maintenance.description: Pick a category and then the exact action to run. Categories are grouped by what you want to achieve: clean your disk, speed up your PC or manage your programs. Nothing runs unless you choose it.
menu.settings.description: Change how Caduceus behaves, or reopen it as administrator. Your choices are saved for the next time.
menu.restart_admin.description:
Opens Caduceus again with administrator rights and closes this console. Windows asks you to confirm first, and if you decline nothing changes. Needed for the options marked [ADMIN].
• Windows · shows its own confirmation window
• This console · closed if started from cmd or PowerShell
maintenance.title: MANUAL MAINTENANCE
maintenance.cleanup.description: Frees up disk space by removing leftovers: temporary files, logs, caches, the Recycle Bin, restore points and previous Windows files. It also holds the hibernation switch, which reserves a large file on your disk. Each option can run on its own, or you can run the fast or the full cleanup in one go.
cleanup.title: DISK CLEANUP
cleanup.temp_and_logs.description:
Removes the temporary files, Windows logs and crash dumps that Windows and programs leave behind. Temporary files from the last {cleanup_age} h and logs from the last {log_age} h are kept (the logs, so there is still something to diagnose problems with), and files in use are skipped. The removed dumps can no longer be used to diagnose those crashes. Windows rebuilds Prefetch, so the first launch of each program may be slightly slower. Most of the system parts need administrator rights.
• Temporary · %TEMP%, C:\Windows\Temp and Prefetch (.pf files)
• Logs · CBS, DISM, Windows Update, Panther and setupapi logs
• Crash dumps · MEMORY.DMP, Minidump, LiveKernelReports and %LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps
cleanup.previous_windows.description:
Permanently deletes what the previous Windows installation and Windows Setup leave on the system drive. It can free many GB, but you can no longer go back to the previous version of Windows, and Setup may not be able to resume or roll back an upgrade. It asks for confirmation first and cannot be cancelled once started. Only available with Safe mode OFF.
• Installation · C:\Windows.old, with the Windows Disk Cleanup
• Upgrade files · %SystemDrive%\$WINDOWS.~BT
• Setup files · %SystemDrive%\$Windows.~WS
cleanup.previous_windows.confirm: This permanently deletes the previous Windows installation (C:\Windows.old) and the Windows Setup folders $WINDOWS.~BT and $Windows.~WS from the system drive. You will no longer be able to go back to the previous version of Windows, Setup and rollback may need these files, and this cannot be undone. Continue only after Windows Setup has finished and you have completed any restart it requested. Once it starts it cannot be cancelled.
cleanup.icon_cache.description:
Restarts Explorer to rebuild icons and thumbnails. The taskbar briefly disappears and open File Explorer windows may close.
• Explorer · iconcache*.db and thumbcache*.db in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer
cleanup.icon_cache.step: Closing Explorer to release its caches
cleanup.components.description:
Frees space from the Windows component store with the official DISM command. It takes minutes, cannot be cancelled once started and may ask for a restart. You can still uninstall updates, and the gain is not estimated.
• Updates · components left by old updates (WinSxS)
cleanup.install_leftovers.setup_running: Windows Setup is in progress. Finish setup before deleting these files.
cleanup.recent_history.description:
Clears your own recent items and Run history. What you pinned yourself is kept: the folders pinned to Quick access and the items pinned to Jump Lists.
• Documents · shortcuts in %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Recent
• Jump Lists · recent items in AutomaticDestinations (pins are kept)
• Run · commands remembered in your RunMRU registry key
cleanup.fast.description:
Runs the quicker cleanups immediately. Save your work in open apps such as Discord, Slack and Teams, which may close.
• Includes · temporary files, logs, crash dumps, caches, recent history and the Recycle Bin
• Skips · Explorer restart, Windows components, restore points and previous Windows files
cleanup.all.description: Runs every cleanup in the list, one after the other, and shows the result of each. It always asks for confirmation, even with Safe mode ON (which skips the actions it blocks). Cannot be cancelled once started and can take several minutes. All the consequences above apply.
cleanup.all.confirm:
Each cleanup runs in order and cannot be cancelled once started.
The Recycle Bin is emptied and recent history and crash dumps are deleted.
Explorer restarts and apps like Discord, Slack and Teams close. Save your work.
With Safe mode OFF, it also deletes restore points and the previous Windows files, which can prevent recovery or rollback. Finish any pending Windows Setup first.
Some cleanups need administrator rights.
cleanup.recycle_bin.description:
Permanently empties the Recycle Bin of every fixed drive. Deleted items cannot be restored afterwards.
• Drives · C:\, D:\ and any other fixed drive
cleanup.components.step: Cleaning the Windows component store (this can take several minutes)
cleanup.windows_old.step: Deleting Windows.old (this can take several minutes)
cleanup.closing_apps.step: Closing the apps that are open
result.admin: Run Caduceus as administrator to clean:
notice.nothing_selectable: Nothing here can be changed right now. Turn Safe mode OFF in Settings, or restart as administrator.
settings.title: SETTINGS
settings.safe_mode.description:
When ON, blocks actions that cannot be undone and put the system at risk. Opens the options to switch it ON or OFF. Your choice is saved.
• Blocked · previous Windows files, restore points, hibernation, startup services, scheduled tasks that are not updaters, uninstalling drivers and runtimes
loading.step: Loading the list (this can take a few seconds)
confirm.title: ARE YOU SURE?
confirm.skipped: Skipped (Safe mode is ON, or it needs administrator):
notice.settings_not_saved: Could not save the setting. It applies until Caduceus closes.
maintenance.performance.description: Manage startup programs and scheduled tasks, switch the power plan, free standby RAM or optimize drives.
cleanup.system_caches.description:
Clears Windows caches and keeps error reports from the past {log_age} h. Windows may download updates again and games may briefly stutter while rebuilding shaders.
• Updates · Windows Update downloads and Delivery Optimization cache
• Reports · WER ReportArchive, ReportQueue and Temp in %LOCALAPPDATA% and %PROGRAMDATA%
• Graphics · DirectX, NVIDIA and AMD shader caches
• Windows · Microsoft Store, Windows Search and INetCache
• Defender · logs and scan cache (quarantine is kept)
• Fonts · font cache (Windows rebuilds it)
• Drivers · NVIDIA and AMD installer leftovers
cleanup.browser_caches.description:
Removes the caches of your web browsers, from every profile. Cookies, passwords, history and extensions are never touched. Pages load slower the first time, and web apps that work offline may need to download their data again. Close the browsers first to free more.
• Chromium · Chrome, Edge, Brave, etc.
• Opera · Opera, Opera GX
• Firefox · every profile
• Contents · pages, code, shaders, etc.
cleanup.app_caches.description:
Removes the caches of apps you use every day. Accounts, messages, notes, settings and downloaded songs and installed games are never touched, and apps that are not installed are ignored. Open chat, work and media apps are force-closed first, so save what you are doing. Code editors, Steam and Epic are never closed. Apps open slower the first time.
• Chat · Discord, Slack, Teams, Signal, etc.
• Work · Notion, Obsidian, Figma
• Dev · VS Code, Cursor, Postman, GitHub Desktop
• Media · Spotify, Adobe (media cache)
• Cloud · OneDrive, Google Drive (logs only)
• Games · Steam, Epic Games, Ubisoft Connect, etc.
cleanup.developer_caches.description:
Removes the package caches of your development tools. Your projects, node_modules and .nuget\packages are not touched. Packages are downloaded again on the next build or install, which fails without network.
• JavaScript · npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun, etc.
• Testing · Playwright, Cypress, etc. (they download again)
• Python · pip, uv, Poetry
• PHP · Composer
• .NET · NuGet, Visual Studio
• Java · Gradle
• Systems · Cargo, Go, Dart
• Games · Unity, Unreal Engine (rebuilding can be slow)
• IDE · JetBrains (projects are indexed again)
cleanup.restore_points.description:
Deletes all restore points and Shadow Copies of the system drive. It can free many GB, but you can no longer go back with a restore point or recover earlier versions of files. It asks for confirmation first and cannot be cancelled once started. Only available with Safe mode OFF.
• Restore · system restore points
• Files · Shadow Copies (previous versions)
cleanup.restore_points.confirm: This permanently deletes ALL the restore points and Shadow Copies of the system drive. You will no longer be able to restore Windows to an earlier point or recover earlier versions of files, and this cannot be undone. Once it starts it cannot be cancelled.
performance.title: PERFORMANCE
performance.startup.description:
Shows the programs that start with Windows, how much memory each one uses right now, and lets you turn each one off or on again. Turning one off only stops it from starting with Windows: it stays installed and nothing is deleted. Services (security, VPN, drivers, databases) can only be changed with Safe mode OFF, and are skipped by the cursor while it is ON.
• Impact · estimated from the memory in use now
• ENTER · switches the selected program ON or OFF
performance.tasks.description:
Shows the scheduled tasks that run when Windows starts or when you sign in (many updaters start this way) and lets you turn each one off or on again. Turning one off only disables the task: it is not deleted. Tasks that are not updaters (security, VPN, drivers) can only be changed with Safe mode OFF, and are skipped by the cursor while it is ON.
• Microsoft · Windows' own tasks are not listed
• Runs at · Logon or Startup
cleanup.hibernation.description:
Shows whether hibernation is ON or OFF and opens the options to switch it. It is a system setting rather than a cleanup, but it frees one of the largest files on the disk, and it can be switched back ON at any time. Only available with Safe mode OFF.
• OFF · frees the space Windows reserves for it
• ON · reserves that space again
cleanup.hibernation.title: HIBERNATION
cleanup.hibernation.off.description:
Turns hibernation off with the official Windows command (powercfg /hibernate off) and frees the space Windows reserves for it. Fast Startup is turned off too. It asks for confirmation first. Only available with Safe mode OFF.
• Hibernation · hiberfil.sys (about 40% of RAM)
• Startup · Fast Startup depends on it
cleanup.hibernation.on.description:
Turns hibernation on with the official Windows command (powercfg /hibernate on). Windows reserves disk space for it again, and Fast Startup becomes available. Only available with Safe mode OFF.
• Hibernation · hiberfil.sys (about 40% of RAM)
cleanup.hibernation.confirm: This turns off hibernation and deletes C:\hiberfil.sys. Fast Startup is turned off too, so Windows may start more slowly, and you can no longer hibernate. To undo it, run powercfg /hibernate on as administrator.
cleanup.restore_points.step: Deleting the restore points (this can take a while)
performance.free_standby.description:
Releases cached pages from the Windows standby list and measures the immediate gain in free RAM.
• Cache · Windows rebuilds it as apps need it
performance.optimize_drives.description:
Shows fixed drives and their capacity and free space. Select a drive with a verified media type to optimize it.
• SSD · TRIM
• HDD · defragmentation
performance.optimize_drives.title: OPTIMIZE DRIVES
performance.optimize_drives.column.name: Drive
performance.optimize_drives.media.unknow:
Windows could not confirm the media type for this drive, so optimization is unavailable.
• Drive · {drive}
performance.optimize_drives.none.descrip: Windows reported no fixed drives with a drive letter.
performance.optimize_drives.failed.descr: The Windows storage service did not return a drive list.
performance.startup.title: STARTUP PROGRAMS
performance.tasks.title: SCHEDULED TASKS
performance.tasks.none.description: No tasks are set to run when Windows starts or when you sign in.
performance.startup.none.description: Windows has no programs registered to start with it.
blocked.unavailable: Dimmed: not available for this program
notice.restart_cancelled: Windows did not give administrator rights, so Caduceus was not restarted.
settings.safe_mode.title: SAFE MODE
settings.safe_mode.on.description:
Blocks actions that cannot be undone and put the system at risk. These options stay dimmed and the cursor skips them.
• Blocked · previous Windows files, restore points, hibernation, startup services, scheduled tasks that are not updaters, uninstalling drivers and runtimes
settings.safe_mode.off.description: Lets you run the actions that Safe mode blocks. Some cannot be undone, so each one still asks for confirmation first. Saved between sessions.
programs.uninstall.stale.confirm:
The uninstaller of this program and the folder it was installed in no longer exist (it was probably deleted by hand), so it cannot be uninstalled. Its entry in the list of installed programs is a leftover, and this removes it. No files are deleted.
A backup of the entry (.reg) is saved first in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Caduceus\removed-entries. Double-click it to restore the entry.
programs.uninstall.backup.step: Saving a backup of the entry
programs.uninstall.step: Waiting for the uninstaller of {name} to close
notice.program_still_installed: The uninstaller has closed, but the program is still installed. It was cancelled, or it is still finishing in another window: once it is done, open the list again.
notice.uninstall_cancelled: Windows did not give the uninstaller administrator rights, so nothing was uninstalled.
notice.uninstaller_not_opened: Windows could not open the uninstaller of this program. It may have been removed already, or the program registered it incorrectly.
performance.power_plan.description:
Opens the power plans you can switch to. The current plan is shown beside the name.
• BALANCED · adjusts performance as needed and reduces power use when the PC is less busy
• HIGH · favours speed at the cost of power use
maintenance.programs.description:
Looks after the programs and apps on your PC, in two parts. Nothing runs unless you choose it.
• Updates · apps that have a newer version, updated one at a time or all together
• Installed programs · repair, reset or uninstall the one you pick
programs.menu.title: PROGRAMS
programs.updates.description:
Lists the apps that have a newer version and updates the ones you choose, one at a time or all together. It uses winget (the Windows package manager), so it only knows the apps winget can find. Nothing runs unless you choose it.
• Lists · the version installed now and the latest
• UPDATE ALL · updates every app in the list, in one go
programs.installed.description:
Shows the programs installed on your PC and the Microsoft Store apps. Pick one and choose what to do with it: repair it or reset it (Microsoft Store apps) or uninstall it (installed programs). What does not apply to it is dimmed.
• Size · as registered by each program (— when unknown)
• Reset · deletes the local data of a Store app, so it asks for confirmation
programs.title: INSTALLED PROGRAMS
programs.none.description: Windows lists no programs or apps on this PC.
programs.reset.confirm: This deletes the local data and settings of the app (you will be signed out of it and anything it kept only on this PC is lost). The app stays installed. This cannot be undone.
performance.power_plan.title: POWER PLAN
performance.power_plan.balanced.descript:
Switches Windows to the Balanced plan.
• Power use · reduces power use when the PC is less busy
performance.power_plan.high.description:
Switches Windows to the High performance plan and creates it from the Windows template if needed. Does not need administrator.
• Power use · may reduce battery life and increase heat
updates.title: UPDATES
updates.update_all.description: Updates every app in the list, one after the other, with the same silent update as choosing them one by one. The result lists what was updated and what failed. It can take a long time. Open apps may be closed to be updated, so save what you are doing first.
updates.none.description: winget found no apps to update. Everything it knows is up to date.
updates.failed.description: winget is not available on this PC, or it did not answer in time, so it is unknown whether there are updates. winget comes with Windows 10 and 11 through the App Installer, which you can install or update from the Microsoft Store. Try again in a moment.
